summary:
Replace the default failure message established through add_action() by storing `str` as the error message to return. This is a better way to display an error because it allows other objects to continue handling the command. Avoid displaying the error with write(): that would require returning 1 unless you want the runtime configuration's `default fail message` to appear after the text written by write(). Returning 1, however, prevents other objects from handling the command.

   If a function pointer is supplied, that function is called. If it returns a string, the string becomes the command-failure message. The function can also use write() if this_player() is set correctly.

   If notify_fail() is called more than once, only the last call takes effect.

   Use this function to provide a more helpful message when a command fails.
